newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia cuts official interest rates.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia cuts official interest rates.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of Australia said on Friday it would cut the official cash interest rate by 0.5 percentage points to 5.5 percent.
Rates were last cut on December 11 when the official cash rate was brought down to 6.0 percent from 6.5 percent.

"Following consideration at the board meeting earlier this month, the bank will operate in the money market today to reduce the cash rate from 6.0 percent to 5.5 percent," the Reserve Bank said. "Underlying inflation has been about two percent over the past year, and the bank's assessment is that it will fall below two percent in coming quarters," the bank said.
"In line with this fall in recorded inflation, measures of inflationary expectations have also fallen in recent months," it said.
Economic activity is picking up from the second half of last year, the bank said.
"Employment growth is still subdued, although forward-looking data suggest some firming in labour-market conditions ahead," the bank said.
"Overall, 1997 looks like being a year of stronger growth than 1996," it said.
The bank said longer-term prospects for growth were also good "and are helped by the ongoing fiscal consolidation confirmed in the recent budget."
"At the same time, this growth does not seem likely to put upward pressure on inflation in the next year or two," it said.

"The above considerations -- namely, inflation forecast to fall below two percent, and economic activity providing scope for further exopansion -- amount to a prima facie case for an easing in policy."

The bank said, however, that such a judgment depended on the longer term outlook for inflation and wages in particular. "Recently, this has been an area of uncertainty as the data have been difficult to interpret and subject to revision," it said.

"The bank's 'on balance' assessment is that the current pace of growth of labour costs, although not yet optimal for an economy with inflation as low as ours, has shown sufficient moderation over the medium term to permit a further easing of policy," the RBA said.
The Industrial Relations Commission's decision on wages had helped in this moderation "and removed one factor which could have pushed up aggregate wages."
Enterprise bargain wage increases appeared to have moderated slightly in recent quarters, the bank said.

"The results of the survey of average weekly earnings, particularly ordinary-time earnings in the latest figures, seem to be consistent with the maintenance of a satisfactory inflation performance," the RBA said.

The bank said that public sector figures and therefore the total figures were almost certainly overstated by compositional distortions. "Our assessment is that earnings growth is approximately four percent and steady, rather than the nearly 4.5 percent and rising that seemed to be the case," it said.

Private sector earnings growth appeared to be a little below that, the bank said. "Our overall assessment of wage bargaining still recognises that some settlements remain higher than seems likely to be sustainable over the longer term, it said.
"Pay settlements of five percent, except in unusual circumstances, are likely to be too high, given our level of unemployment," it added.
